values.note: Mostly tent sites; the trailer-capable sites are rated 15-20 ft except site 62 (28 ft, pop-up/tent type), the only one a 23-ft rig fits. Loop A takes self-contained units only, 25 ft or less. A 6-ton bridge limit applies to sites 28-78. Also 4 yurts and 3 group sites.

note: MA DCR state forest in Baldwinville, the first campground in the Massachusetts state park system (1915), set in CCC-planted pines around two-acre Beaman Pond (swimming). Mountain biking in the adjacent 9,000-acre Birch Hill WMA. Only one vehicle per site (overflow lot at the contact station). Nearest dump station is at Lake Dennison Recreation Area. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on ReserveAmerica + mass.gov: $17/$54, no hookups, showers + flush toilets, 6-ton bridge limit on sites 28-78 (EKKO ~5.5 t passes), 73 sites + 4 yurts + 3 group sites, season 5/14-9/6, phone 978-939-8962. Changed max_rig_ft 25 -> 28 (RA site 062) and dump -> false (dump station is at Lake Dennison). Added flush toilets, back-in only, fcfs never, 14-day limit, RA url. Note cleaned. See criteria flag: only one site fits a 23-ft rig.
flags: Criteria (rig length - possible drop, AWH's call): RA singles this campground out: 'Most sites are small and tight only small self contained units must be 25` or less' (Loop A). RA's site catalog rates every trailer-capable site 15-20 ft except site 062 (28 ft, POPUP/TENT type, beyond the 6-ton bridge, which EKKO passes at ~5.5 tons). The old note's 'site 33' is rated 15 ft. So exactly one of 73 sites takes a 23-ft rig.

Walk-ins conflict: mass.gov says 'Walk-in campsite reservations are allowed, but it is recommended that you call ahead to check availability', while RA says 'RESERVATIONS REQUIRED. NO WALK-IN CAMPING ALLOWED' and 'Walk-in Registrations are not permitted. Advance Reservations can be made same day up until 2 pm'. Kept fcfs never per RA. mass.gov also says 76 campsites vs RA's 73.

Waterfront re-audit lead (stored not waterfront; not changed): RA says the campground is 'situated around two-acre Beaman Pond', but tags only the day-use pavilion Near Water, and no 23-ft-capable site.
